text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein to meet U.S. President Clinton in Washington in March.
- Philadelphia Bank BANK.AM to issue 10 million new shares to raise capital to Central Bank's minimum requirement of 20 million dinars ($28.2 million).

- Parliament passes 18 articles of new companies law, which aims to encourage investment and open up economy. Deputies seek government statement on Jordanian prisoners in Kuwait who were reportedly beaten.
- Telecommunications authorities look into cutting costs of calls during Eid holidays.
- Syria would welcome any Jordanian initiative to help peace talks with Israel, Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam says in Muscat.
- King Hussein stresses importance of true democracy.
- Labour Minister Shakhanbeh says there will be lots of work opportunities for Jordanians in Saudi Arabia this year.
- Trade and Industry Minister Abu al-Ragheb says Jordan will reply in March to WTO questions over its application for membership. Says Jordan seeks 10-year period to bring customs duties into line.
- King urges democratic practices that do not harm national unity.
- Five Jordanian prisoners in hospital after reported Kuwaiti beating.
